newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubin to be told Japan seeks domestic-led growth.
newsitem.headline: Rubin to be told Japan seeks domestic-led growth.

text.p: Japan will tell U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that Japan will aim for stable economic growth centring on domestic demand, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Thursday.

Asked how Japan planned to respond to Rubin's expected request that Japan not depend too much on exports for economic growth, Ogawa said: "We will explain our basic ideas on economic management. We want to pursue stable economic management centring on domestic demand."
He added: "Looking at current economic conditions and future prospects, we would like to explain that Japan's economy is being supported by private demand and its gait is firm."

Ogawa added that for medium- to long-term stable economic management, both fiscal and economic structural reform needed to be carried out in Japan and he hoped to gain understanding from the U.S. side on that.

"Overall the economy has a firm gait centring on domestic demand and I have no doubt that the massive trade surplus, which is a source of worry, will not expand as rapidly as it did previously," he said.
Asked how Japan and the United States would evaluate the foreign exchange market, Ogawa said: "There is no change from the ideas expressed at the Group of Seven (G7) meeting (in February)."
The G7 nations agreed in Berlin in February that major misalignments in exchange rates, noted in the G7's April 1995 communique, had been corrected.

They also affirmed that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excess volatility is undesirable. They agreed to monitor developments in currency markets and to coooperate as appropriate.
